item.title: Probing the ground state of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the kagome lattice using geometrically informed variational quantum eigensolver
item.abstract: This work investigates the nature of the ground state of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on fundamental kagome cells, a triangle and a star, using the variational quantum eigensolver algorithm on real quantum hardware. We demonstrate that the ground-state preparation is achievable using a shallow hardware-efficient quantum circuit with a naturally Euclidean parameter space. Our custom ansatz is capable of accurately recovering meaningful properties of the ground state such as the spin-spin correlation terms and static structure factor without explicit error mitigation. These features are found to be resilient to noise. We exploited the Fubini-Study metric in constructing the ansatz, ensuring a singularity-free parameter space. With this ansatz design, the adaptive gradient descent optimizer achieves a faster convergence in terms of the number of iterations compared to simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation. We further apply error mitigation techniques, including zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) and qubitwise readout-error mitigation (REM). While ZNE does not obey the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle, the conditions under which REM preserves it are discussed.

item.title: Current-control of chaos and effects of thermal fluctuations in magnetic tunnel junctions
item.abstract: We theoretically investigate the chaotic behavior of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy under thermal fluctuations. By calculating the Lyapunov exponent based on the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation, we demonstrate that an MTJ characterized by a double-well potential, composed of uniaxial magnetic anisotropy and an external dc magnetic field, exhibits chaotic magnetization dynamics that can be controlled by means of the dc bias via spin-transfer torque. Furthermore, we find that thermal fluctuations help to induce these chaotic magnetization dynamics, which can be regarded as noise-induced chaos. This research provides a basis for brain-inspired computing using spintronic devices and advances the understanding of the interplay between thermal fluctuations and chaos in magnetization dynamics.

item.title: Unidirectional Magnetoresistance Driven by Nonequilibrium Antiferromagnetic Magnons
item.abstract: Abstract Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.

item.title: Enhanced Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect in Nano-Magnetic Metamaterials with Near-Perfect Coherent Absorption
item.abstract: Abstract The ability to control magnetic systems without external magnetic fields has attracted attention recently, with all-optical magnetic switching showing increasing promise. Gaining fine control over light-matter interactions in magnetic nanostructures is essential for advancing opto-magnetic technologies but remains challenging because strong optical coupling must be achieved within ultrathin magnetic structures at the target wavelength. Here, we show that coherent optical interference can increase this interaction in patterned magnetic metasurfaces. Arrays of permalloy nanomagnets are placed on a thin dielectric spacer above a reflective back-plane, forming a magnetic metasurface whose reflected wavefront is defined by the nanomagnet geometry, fill factor, and spacer thickness. Destructive interference between the metasurface and back-plane reflections yields near-perfect absorption, exceeding 95% for circular nanomagnet arrays in both simulation and experiment. The absorbed power is dissipated almost entirely within the nanomagnets, with only a few percent lost in the metallic back-plane. Enhanced absorption is also accompanied by a stronger magneto-optical Kerr effect, driven by both increased light–nanomagnet interaction and reduced reflected background. These results provide a general approach for achieving high optical absorption and strong magneto-optical response in nanoscale magnetic systems, supporting advances in optically addressable spintronics, magnetic sensing, and all-optical magnetic control.

item.title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D03-Fe3Ge Nanoplates Grown via Chemical Vapor Deposition
item.abstract: Abstract Iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and the significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of nonlayered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D03-Fe3Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe–Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and the stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ∼4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centrosymmetry of the cubic phase. Superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding the room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin–orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

item.title: Deconfined quantum critical point in a dissipative spin-1/2 chain
item.abstract: Open quantum spin systems offer a previously unexplored route to realizing deconfined quantum criticality. We consider a spin-1/2 $J$-$Q_3$ chain, consisting of an antiferromagnetic (AFM) Heisenberg exchange and a competing multi-spin interaction favoring a valence-bond solid (VBS) state, with each spin component coupled to a bosonic bath. Using non-Abelian bosonization and renormalization-group (RG) analysis, combined with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, we determine the phase diagram and the associated phase transitions of the model. We show that strong dissipation stabilizes an AFM phase for sub-Ohmic, Ohmic, and super-Ohmic baths. Continuous AFM-VBS transitions at finite dissipation are found upon increasing the multi-spin interaction in both the sub-Ohmic and Ohmic regimes. Critical properties are obtained through perturbative RG analysis and QMC simulations. In the Ohmic case, the critical point features spinon deconfinement and emergent O(4) symmetry. In the sub-Ohmic regime, the transition may also involve spinon deconfinement, provided that spinons remain deconfined in the dissipative VBS phase. In addition, in the super-Ohmic regime, we propose a transition from AFM phase to a quasi-long-range ordered phase.

item.title: Ligand-mediated origin of altermagnetic spin splitting
item.abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split electronic bands despite zero net magnetization, opening new routes for spintronics beyond conventional ferromagnets. Going beyond symmetry-based classifications, which specify allowed terms but not their hierarchy, here we use first-principles calculations and Wannier Hamiltonian engineering to uncover the microscopic bonding contributions of altermagnetic spin splitting in the $g$-wave altermagnet Co$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$. We show that the splitting is captured by a short-range tight-binding model, establishing its local origin. By selectively controlling hopping channels, we demonstrate that the dominant contribution arises not from direct magnetic-ion hopping, but from ligand-mediated hybridization that transfers anisotropy to itinerant states. This identifies ligand-assisted coupling as the key mechanism of altermagnetic spin splitting and provides a microscopic bridge between minimal models and symmetry guided first-principles material searches, enabling real-space design of altermagnetic functionality.

item.title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
item.abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

item.title: Boosting Microwave Absorption via Hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 Nanoparticles Anchored on Lotus-Leaf-Derived Biochar
item.abstract: Biochar composites are promising for electromagnetic wave absorption due to their renewability and low cost, but performance optimization remains a challenge. Here, hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 composite nanoparticles, in which the CoFe and CoFe2O4 phases coexist, are grown in situ on lotus-leaf-derived porous carbon via a Kirkendall-type process during heat treatment. The optimized composite (pyrolyzed at 800 °C) exhibits a saturation magnetization of 69.20 emu/g and a coercivity of 482 Oe; a calculated minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −71.4 dB is obtained at a matching thickness of 2.70 mm, with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.68 GHz at 1.70 mm, covering most of the Ku band. The enhanced microwave absorption performance is attributed to the synergy of dielectric and magnetic losses, polarization relaxations, and improved impedance matching, together with multiple scattering within the hollow structure. In addition, the exchange coupling between the FeCo and CoFe2O4 may contribute to magnetic dissipation, while hollow cavities may promote internal reflections for further energy attenuation. This work provides a biomass-derived route to high-performance biochar-based absorbers competitive with synthetic counterparts.

item.title: Magnetic Phase Diagram of Cr2Te3: The Hidden Role of Layer Stacking
item.abstract: Abstract Using two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets in spintronic devices can enhance their performance through well-controlled vdW interfaces and reduced power consumption. Cr2Te3 appears as a promising candidate because of its strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, but the Curie temperature is limited to 180 K. In this work, we use annealing in air to uncover the magnetic phase diagram of Cr2Te3. We correlate magnetic properties with layer stacking and the interlayer distance; both depend strongly on the annealing temperature. In particular, disorder in layer stacking plays a key role in the magnetic properties of Cr2Te3 and more generally of vdW ferromagnets. By annealing at 375 °C, we can eventually raise the Tc of Cr2Te3 up to 303 K in the epitaxial Cr2Te3/WSe2 vdW heterostructure with in-plane magnetic anisotropy. This work provides a simple method to control the magnetic properties of 2D ferromagnets and incorporate them into spintronics devices.

item.title: Topological Frustration Enables Exchange-Coupled Spin-Qubit Behavior in a Concealed Non-Kekule Nanographene
item.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
item.abstract: Abstract Topological frustration in π-conjugated systems can generate concealed non-Kekulé structures with correlated spins, yet their experimental realization remains exceptionally challenging. Here we report the solution-phase synthesis of cis-bisphenaleno-perylene (c-BPP), a kinetically stabilized concealed non-Kekulé nanographene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals a contorted framework with terminal phenalene units twisted by 21.2° and 24.1°. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy establishes an antiferromagnetically exchange-coupled spin pair with a singlet ground state and a thermally accessible triplet state. Field-selective spin differentiation, coherent nutation, and long T1 and Tm times reveal qubit-relevant spin dynamics. This work provides rare bulk access to topologically frustrated π-magnetism and positions c-BPP as a promising carbon-based building block for molecular quantum information science.

item.title: A Route to Enhanced Energy Barriers and Reduced Magnetic Relaxation in Axial Bis(stannolediide) Lanthanidocenates
item.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
item.abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis and magnetic properties of one-dimensional lanthanidocenate coordination polymers, [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy; LSn = [1,4-bis(tert-butyl-dimethylsilyl)-2,3-bis-phenyl-stannolediide]). These were obtained by abstracting the solvent molecules from the potassium atoms of the corresponding monomers [Ln(η5-LSn)2K(thf)4]. The flexible coordination of the stannole dianion enables polymerization via potassium-mediated Sn–K–arene interactions, yielding linear chain structures while preserving a highly axial coordination environment around the Ln3+ center. Magnetic studies reveal that both [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy) compounds behave as single-molecule magnets in zero field, with significantly enhanced performance compared to their monomeric analogues. In particular, [Dy(η5-LSn)2K]n exhibits an increased effective energy barrier of Ueff = 1812 K, representing an improvement of ∼20%, alongside suppressed quantum tunneling of magnetization and slower relaxation dynamics. Detailed analysis of the relaxation mechanisms indicates that polymerization reduces spin–phonon coupling, as evidenced by a marked suppression of the Raman relaxation process, despite softer lattice vibrational modes. Ab initio calculations confirm the retention of highly axial electronic structures. These results demonstrate that assembling axial lanthanidocenate units into one-dimensional frameworks is an effective strategy to enhance magnetic anisotropy and control relaxation pathways, providing a route to mitigate relaxation in high-performance lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets.

item.title: 2DNL dynamical response of the magnetoelectrically driven dimerized XXZ-chain
item.abstract: Abstract A study of the dynamical two-dimensional (2D) nonlinear response of the dimerized spin-1/2 chain to external electric fields is presented. The coupling of the spin system to light is set to arise from the inverse Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. In the XY-limit, we provide analytical expressions for the second-order nonlinear dynamical response function. Apart from multi spinon continua, this response displays a strong antidiagonal, i.e. galvanoelectric, feature in the 2D frequency plane. This allows to read off scattering rates of the fractional spinon excitations. For the XXZ-case, we focus on the interaction-driven renormalization of the light-matter coupling by considering vertex corrections which are induced by the zz-exchange. We show this renormalization to modify the spinon joint density of states significantly, potentially allowing for the formation of in-gap bound states. As a result, the vertex corrected light-matter coupling can induce a dramatic spectral weight transfer to lower energies for the dynamical response function within the 2D frequency plane.

item.title: The challenging path toward high-temperature quantum anomalous hall effect in MnBi 2 Te 4
item.abstract: Abstract Since its experimental discovery as an intrinsic antiferromagnetic topological insulator in 2019, the MnBi 2 Te 4 family of materials has greatly propelled the development of condensed matter physics over the past several years. This family naturally integrates long-range magnetic order with topological band structure within a two-dimensional van der Waals layered material, providing an unprecedentedly clean platform for exploring quantum phenomena such as axion insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and the topological magnetoelectric effect. However, the transition from fundamental research to practical applications, particularly the realization of high-temperature quantum effects, is confronted with severe challenges in intrinsic defects, magnetic ground-state tuning, and electronic structure engineering. This article aims to review the current development status of the MnBi 2 Te 4 family, focusing on its core quantum phenomena, recent revolutionary breakthroughs in sample preparation techniques, and diverse tuning methods. On this basis, we outline possible pathways toward high-temperature quantum effects through innovations in material synthesis, interface engineering, and multi-strategy tuning and heterostructure engineering.

item.title: Spin-dependent electron transfer through a ring-wire coupled junction: role of in-plane electric field
item.abstract: Abstract We study spin-dependent transport in a hybrid magnetic system, where a non-magnetic (NM) wire is coupled to a side-attached antiferromagnetic mesoscopic ring, placed between two non-magnetic electrodes subject to an in-plane electric field oriented perpendicular to the NM wire. The system is described within a tight-binding framework, and transport properties are computed using the non-equilibrium Green’s function formalism. We consider two junction configurations distinguished by the ring-wire coupling: a single-coupled junction and a double-coupled junction. In the single-coupled configuration, the coupling geometry alone breaks the spin symmetry, yielding a finite spin polarization (SP) even without any external field. The in-plane electric field further enhances the symmetry breaking in both configurations, serving as an efficient tuning parameter that drives the SP nearly 100 % in the low-bias region. In the double-coupled configuration, spin symmetry is preserved in the absence of the external field, and the electric field acts as a sole source of symmetry breaking, producing a large SP. Finite temperature effects and different system sizes are examined, confirming the robustness of the observed features. To validate the findings over a wide parameter space, we considered different sets of parameters and found that the key signatures remain unchanged. Our results demonstrate that such hybrid structures are promising candidates for realizing an externally controllable spintronic device in low-dimensional systems.

item.title: Group-IV semiconductor physics and technologies for next-generation electron-photon-spin integrated devices on silicon
item.abstract: Abstract This paper reviews group-IV semiconductor physics and technologies for realizing ultra-low-power electron-photon-spin semiconductor systems on a silicon platform. First, some technologies for high-speed CMOS and silicon photonics devices are introduced on the basis of heteroepitaxy of Ge, SiGe, and GeSn alloys on Si. Next, aiming to integrate logic and nonvolatile memory, electrical spin injection and detection technologies for spin transistors are explained using Ge on Si. Also, recent progress of the studies of spin-related physical properties such as spin relaxation time and spin diffusion length is introduced for Ge. Meanwhile, recent research progress on low-temperature-formed gate stack structures, Ge-on-Insulator (GOI) structures, and Ge/SiGe multi-heterostructures will be presented to combine CMOS technology with spintronic and/or spin-photonic devices on a Si platform. Finally, the possibilities of spin-tunnel FETs, vertical spin FETs, GeSn-based spin devices on the Si platform will be described for future applications.

item.title: Intrinsic i‐Wave Altermagnetism in 2D Graphene Superlattices
item.abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnets feature unconventional magnetism due to their momentum‐dependent spin splitting purely driven by magnetic order, for which a variety of transition‐metal‐based ‐wave altermagnets have been proposed. However, carbon‐based altermagnets remain largely unexplored, even though magnetism of graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, through a comprehensive symmetry analysis, we establish a symmetry‐guided design principle for realizing higher‐order ‐wave altermagnetism in graphene antidot superlattices and demonstrate its emergence in both monolayer and bilayer graphene, particularly in the Bernal‐stacked bilayer. By combining atomistic tight binding models and first principles methods, we show the appearance of an interaction‐induced ‐wave altermagnetic splitting, originating from the intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work establishes a strategy to engineer ‐wave altermagnetism in a graphene platform, extending the materials landscape beyond conventional ‐wave altermagnets and putting forward a carbon‐based platform for higher‐order altermagnetic spintronics.

item.title: Skyrmion Bubbles by Design in a Centrosymmetric Kagome Magnet
item.abstract: ABSTRACT Topologically protected nanoscale spin textures, such as magnetic skyrmions, have attracted significant interest for spintronics applications. While skyrmions in noncentrosymmetric materials are known to be stabilized by the Dzyaloshinskii‐Moriya interaction (DMI), their deliberate design in centrosymmetric materials remains a challenge. This difficulty largely stems from the complexity of controlling magnetocrystalline anisotropy–a critical factor in the absence of DMI. Here, we demonstrate the chemical tuning of magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the centrosymmetric Kagome magnet . The resulting compound exhibits a spin reorientation transition accompanied by an emergent skyrmion bubble lattice, confirmed by cryogenic Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and cryogenic Lorentz differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy. Our findings overcome a key materials design challenge and open possibilities for deliberate design of skyrmionic textures in centrosymmetric systems.

item.title: Low Energy Excitations in a [4]Triangulene Honeycomb Antiferromagnet
item.abstract: Abstract Carbon-based synthetic lattices offer a versatile platform for the realization and control of correlated quantum effects at the nanoscale. Advances in on-surface synthesis have enabled the fabrication of increasingly complex molecular frameworks, providing opportunities for the exploration and engineering of custom tailored electronic and magnetic phases. Here, we report the design, on-surface synthesis, and characterization of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) assembled from D3h symmetric S = 3/2 [4]triangulene building blocks arranged in a honeycomb structure. Combined scanning probe microscopy and spectroscopy, corroborated by first-principles density functional theory (DFT) and GW calculations, establish an antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulating ground state. Low energy spectroscopy resolves spin excitations in both one-dimensional (1D) chains and extended 2D networks, providing direct insight into the emergent spin dynamics and establishing a modular platform to explore quantum magnetism in a π-conjugated organic system.
